application_credentials.description: The integration signs in with the project's own published Cloudflare OAuth client; nothing needs to be added here. To sign in through a client of your own instead, create it in the Cloudflare dashboard under Manage Account → OAuth clients with redirect URL `{redirect_uri}`, grant types authorization code and refresh token, token endpoint authentication none (PKCE) and the scopes {scopes}, and enter its client ID here with an empty secret; it then takes the project's client's place. [Details]({more_info_url}).

user.title: Cloudflare Access
user.description: The integration creates and maintains an Access application that gates the whole hostname, lets in the people who have a Home Assistant account, and serves as the OAuth server for token-bearing clients. Continue to sign in with Cloudflare; the consent page shows the three permissions the integration uses.

account.title: Cloudflare account
account.description: The sign-in reaches several accounts. Choose the one whose zone serves the hostname.

api_token.title: Cloudflare API token
api_token.description: An account-level token with the permissions 'Access: Apps and Policies: Edit' and 'Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups: Read'. Stored in the config entry.

settings.title: Hostname and options
settings.description: The gate starts disabled: nothing changes at the edge until you enable it in the options. Its allow policy lists the e-mail addresses of the Home Assistant users (currently: {allowed_users}) and follows them as users come and go.

data.service_token_ids: Service token IDs allowed through the gate
data.client_redirect_uris: Redirect URIs allowed for self-registering clients
data.delete_objects_on_remove: Delete the Access applications when the integration is removed

data_description.hostname: The public hostname served through Cloudflare, e.g. ha.example.com.
data_description.service_token_ids: IDs of Access service tokens (Zero Trust → Access → Service auth) that may pass the gate with CF-Access-Client-Id/Secret headers, as a Service Auth policy.
data_description.session_duration: Lifetime of an Access session, e.g. 720h. Also the lifetime of a registered client's refresh token.
data_description.client_redirect_uris: Clients that discover the OAuth server themselves (MCP clients such as Claude) register with Access dynamically; Access accepts their registration only if their redirect URI is listed here. https:// URLs, optionally ending in /* for all sub-paths. Clients with a console that asks for a client id and secret are registered instead under this entry's "Add OAuth client".
data_description.extra_bypass_paths: Hostname-relative path prefixes that must stay reachable without Access, e.g. /api/webhook/abc for a third-party service that can hold neither cookie nor bearer. Nothing is bypassed unless listed here.
data_description.identity_claim: Claim of the Access assertion compared with the Home Assistant user, usually email.
data_description.user_match: Which Home Assistant user field holds the e-mail address: 'username' (built-in login), 'name' (display name), or any credential field such as 'email' for OIDC providers. The same field feeds the allow policy and matches an admitted identity to the user.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in with Cloudflare again
reauth_confirm.description: Cloudflare no longer accepts the sign-in. Continue to sign in again.

error.invalid_auth: Cloudflare rejected the credential. It needs 'Access: Apps and Policies: Edit' on this account.
error.missing_org_read: The credential cannot read the Zero Trust organization (the team domain). It needs 'Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups: Read'.
error.api_error: Cloudflare returned an error; see the log.
error.invalid_hostname: Enter a hostname such as ha.example.com.
error.invalid_redirect_uri: Redirect URIs must start with https://.

abort.invalid_auth: Cloudflare rejected the credential. It needs 'Access: Apps and Policies: Edit' on this account.
abort.missing_org_read: The credential cannot read the Zero Trust organization (the team domain). It needs 'Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups: Read'.
abort.api_error: Cloudflare returned an error; see the log.
abort.no_accounts: The sign-in reaches no Cloudflare account.

init.title: Cloudflare Access for {hostname}
init.description: Changing an option re-provisions the Access applications (reload the integration to re-provision without a change). Enabling the gate is the exposure change: the whole hostname then requires an Access session, except the bypassed paths listed here. The allow policy lists the e-mail addresses of the Home Assistant users (currently: {allowed_users}) and follows them as users come and go.

restart_required.title: Restart Home Assistant to accept clients authenticated by Cloudflare Access
restart_required.description: The integration was set up after the web server had started, so its authentication middleware could not be installed. Until Home Assistant is restarted, requests from token-bearing clients (Google Assistant, Alexa, MCP clients) that Cloudflare Access admitted are rejected by Home Assistant.

no_allowed_users.title: No Home Assistant user can pass the Cloudflare Access gate
no_allowed_users.description: No active Home Assistant user has an e-mail address in the field the options name ({user_match}), so there is nobody to list in the gate's allow policy. The policy was left as it was. Give a user an address, or change the field in the options.

user.title: Register an OAuth client
user.description: For a client whose console asks for a client id and secret (Google Home account linking, the Alexa skill, any service that cannot register itself). Access issues the credentials; the next page shows them together with the authorization and token URLs to enter in that console. Who may link the client is the gate's own allow rule.

data_description.name: Anything that identifies the client to you, e.g. Google Home.
data_description.redirect_uris: The callback URL(s) the client's console shows. Exact https:// URLs.

reconfigure.title: Change the OAuth client
reconfigure.description: Saving updates the registration in Access and shows the credentials again.
